//: Benchmark manifest — DATA, not code. Add/remove/rename models here; the
JSON, not YAML, DELIBERATELY. PyYAML is absent on this host and the repo's
yaml-dependent tests run inside the LiteLLM container to get it. This
harness cannot: it must control Ollama model residency and read host memory
and swap, which are not visible from inside a container. Zero dependencies
beats a hand-rolled parser for a nested document.
FAIRNESS BASELINE, applied to every model. temperature 0 makes runs
reproducible and comparable -- but it is OFF-SPEC for every vendor here.
See model_settings for what each vendor actually recommends, and run with
--vendor-settings to measure a model at its documented best. Comparisons
across models are only valid WITHIN one setting regime, never across.
Vendor-recommended knobs, recorded as DATA. Not applied by default: mixing
per-model sampling into a cross-model comparison measures the settings as
much as the models. Use --vendor-settings for a per-model-best run and
compare it against the fixed-params run, never against the other regime.

qwen3.5:9b.note: Vendor recommends 32768 output for most queries. Our 8192 ceiling may truncate long thinking.

qwen3-coder:30b-a3b-q4_K_M.note: No thinking capability (probe confirmed rejection). Non-thinking settings only.

gpt-oss:20b.note: The native effort control is a SYSTEM-PROMPT directive, not a sampling param. This likely explains why Ollama's think:false does not silence it (measured 111 reasoning chars with think=false).

measured.conclusion: The SYSTEM-PROMPT lever gives three distinct monotonic levels; Ollama's think gives only two (off and standard identical, i.e. off is ignored). For gpt-oss the vendor control is strictly better.
